title: 1.1. Fundamentals of Computer Programming
summary: Explore how computers process information, how machine code interacts with hardware, and why high-level programming languages were invented.
learningObjectives: Explain the fundamental architecture of a computer (CPU, RAM, Storage, and I/O devices).
Differentiate between machine language, assembly language, and high-level programming languages.
Understand what a computer program is: an ordered sequence of unambiguous instructions.

sections.heading: 1.1.1 How Does a Computer Program Work?
sections.content:
A computer is an astonishingly fast electronic machine, but it possesses zero independent intelligence. At its core, a central processing unit (CPU) can only perform a very limited set of fundamental operations: fetching data from memory, performing simple arithmetic (addition, subtraction), performing boolean comparisons (is X greater than Y?), and branching to another instruction based on the result.

A computer program is a set of instructions that dictates how the CPU should transform inputs into desired outputs. The language directly understood by hardware is machine code — composed entirely of binary digits (0s and 1s) representing electrical voltage states.

Because writing complex software directly in binary or assembly is tedious and error-prone, computer scientists designed high-level programming languages like Python, allowing developers to write instructions in human-readable notation.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is the only language that a computer CPU can execute directly without translation?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: CPUs execute machine code (binary electrical instructions) directly on silicon transistors.

recap: Computers execute machine code; high-level languages like Python abstract hardware details into expressive human-readable logic.
